classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied progression to evaluate tangent and normal gradients, construct both lines, select their specified axis intercepts and form the right-triangle area. The geometry and target are explicit, so no unsignposted connection is required.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $y=3\cos^2 x$ has derivative $y'=-6\sin x\cos x$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the gradients of the tangent and normal to $y=3\cos^2 x$ at the point where $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.

answer.worked:
At $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$:
$$\begin{align*}y'&=-6\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\\&=-6\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)\\&=-3.\end{align*}$$
Gradient of tangent $=-3$.

Gradient of normal $=-\frac{1}{-3}=\frac13$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the equations of the tangent and normal to $y=3\cos^2 x$ at the point where $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Suppose that the tangent meets the $x$-axis at $P$, the normal meets the $y$-axis at $Q$ and $O$ is the origin. Show that $\triangle OPQ$ has area $\frac{(\pi+2)(18-\pi)}{96}$ units$^2$.

answer.worked:
The tangent $3x+y=\frac{3\pi}{4}+\frac32$ meets the $x$-axis where $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac12,\\P&=\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac12,0\right).\end{align*}$$
The normal $x-3y=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac92$ meets the $y$-axis where $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac32-\frac{\pi}{12},\\Q&=\left(0,\frac32-\frac{\pi}{12}\right).\end{align*}$$
Since the coordinate axes are perpendicular,
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OPQ)&=\frac12|OP||OQ|\\&=\frac12\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac12\right)\left(\frac32-\frac{\pi}{12}\right)\\&=\frac12\left(\frac{\pi+2}{4}\right)\left(\frac{18-\pi}{12}\right)\\&=\frac{(\pi+2)(18-\pi)}{96}\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$
